heat-transfer.text: In an experiment, four pins (I, II, III, IV) are attached with wax in a line along a metal strip. If the end near pin I is heated, what will be observed?
options: The pins will fall in the order I, then II, then III, then IV.
The pins will not fall at all.
All pins will fall at the same time.
heat-transfer.explanation: Heat is transferred by conduction from the hot end along the strip, melting the wax for each pin in sequence from nearest to farthest.

heat-transfer.text: Why do two thin blankets often feel warmer than one single thick blanket?
options: The material of thin blankets is warmer.
The air trapped between the two blankets acts as an insulator.
Thick blankets allow heat to escape.
heat-transfer.explanation: Air is a poor conductor of heat, so the layer of air trapped between two blankets reduces heat flow from our bodies to the surroundings.

heat-transfer.text: What happens to air when it gets heated, for example, by a candle flame?
options: It expands, becomes lighter, and rises.
heat-transfer.explanation: When air is heated, it expands, occupies more space, becomes lighter, and rises up.

heat-transfer.text: The process of heat transfer that involves the actual movement of particles, which occurs in liquids and gases, is called:
heat-transfer.explanation: Convection is the process of heat transfer where the entire volume of a liquid or gas gets heated through the actual movement of its particles.

heat-transfer.text: During the day in a coastal area, a cool breeze blows from the sea to the land. What is this phenomenon called?
heat-transfer.explanation: The movement of cooler air from the sea to the land during the day is called a sea breeze.

heat-transfer.text: At night in coastal areas, a breeze blows from the land to the sea. What is this called?
heat-transfer.explanation: At night, land cools down faster than the sea, so cooler air from the land moves towards the sea, creating a land breeze.

heat-transfer.text: Why is it more comfortable to wear dark-coloured clothes in winter?
options: They reflect most of the heat.
They are thicker than light clothes.
heat-transfer.explanation: Dark surfaces absorb more heat than light-coloured surfaces, which helps to keep us feel more comfortable during winters.

heat-transfer.text: In the water cycle, what is the process of water turning into water vapour due to heat from the Sun called?
heat-transfer.explanation: Water in oceans, rivers, and lakes gets heated by the Sun and evaporates as water vapour.

heat-transfer.text: Rain, snow, and hail are all forms of which process in the water cycle?
heat-transfer.explanation: When water vapour in clouds cools and condenses, it falls back to Earth as rain, snow, or hail, a process called precipitation.

heat-transfer.text: The process of surface water seeping through soil and rocks to become groundwater is called:
heat-transfer.explanation: Infiltration is the process of surface water seeping through soil and rocks.

heat-transfer.text: Underground layers of sediments and rocks that store water in their pore spaces are known as:
heat-transfer.explanation: Aquifers are the underground layers of sediments and rocks that store water in pore spaces.

heat-transfer.text: If you compare the seepage of water through clay, sand, and gravel, through which material will water seep the slowest?
options: It is the same for all three.
heat-transfer.explanation: Water seeps slowest through clay because the spaces between its particles are smaller compared to those in sand and gravel.

heat-transfer.text: Which of these materials is a good conductor of heat?
heat-transfer.explanation: Copper is a metal, and metals allow heat to pass through them easily.

heat-transfer.text: Which mode of heat transfer mainly takes place in solids?
heat-transfer.explanation: In solids, heat passes from particle to particle without the particles moving from their places, which is conduction.

heat-transfer.text: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
heat-transfer.explanation: The space between the Sun and the Earth has almost no particles, so heat reaches us by radiation, which needs no medium.

heat-transfer.text: Why are the handles of pressure cookers and frying pans usually made of plastic or wood?
options: Plastic and wood are poor conductors, so the handle does not get very hot
Plastic and wood are good conductors, so food cooks faster
Plastic and wood make the pan heat up quickly
Plastic and wood absorb all the heat of the flame
heat-transfer.explanation: Plastic and wood are insulators, so very little heat travels through them to our hands.

heat-transfer.text: Why are ventilators or exhaust openings in a room usually placed near the ceiling?
options: Cool air rises and escapes from the top
Ventilators let in more sunlight from the top
Warm air rises and can escape through openings near the top
heat-transfer.explanation: Warm air is lighter, so it rises and goes out through openings near the ceiling while fresh cooler air comes in from below.

heat-transfer.text: When water in a pot is heated from below, why does the hot water at the bottom move upward?
options: Hot water becomes heavier and is pushed up
Hot water becomes lighter and rises, while cooler water sinks
The flame pushes the water upward
Hot water turns into ice and floats
heat-transfer.explanation: Heated water becomes lighter and rises while cooler, heavier water moves down to take its place, setting up convection currents.

heat-transfer.text: On a sunny day in a coastal area, which gets heated faster?
options: Both get heated at exactly the same rate
Neither gets heated by the Sun
heat-transfer.explanation: Land heats up faster than water, so on a sunny day the land becomes warmer than the sea.

heat-transfer.text: What is meant by the water table?
options: The upper level of groundwater, below which the soil and rocks are filled with water
A table used to record daily rainfall
The level of water in a river during floods
The height of clouds above the ground
heat-transfer.explanation: The water table is the top surface of the underground zone in which all the spaces in soil and rocks are filled with water.

heat-transfer.text: What happens during condensation in the water cycle?
options: Water from the ground seeps down into the soil
Water falls from clouds as rain
Water vapour cools and changes into tiny droplets of water
Ice melts into water on mountains
heat-transfer.explanation: When water vapour high in the air cools, it condenses into tiny droplets that together form clouds.

heat-transfer.text: In which of these situations is heat transferred mainly by radiation?
options: A steel spoon getting hot when kept in hot tea
Water in a pan getting heated from the bottom
Your hand getting hot when you touch a hot iron
Feeling warmth on your face while sitting beside a bonfire
heat-transfer.explanation: Heat from a bonfire reaches a person sitting beside it mainly by radiation, since warm air rises upward and air is a poor conductor.

heat-transfer.text: How does covering open ground with concrete and tar roads affect groundwater?
options: It increases groundwater because concrete stores rainwater
It reduces groundwater because less rainwater can seep into the ground
It has no effect on groundwater
It makes groundwater turn into water vapour
heat-transfer.explanation: Concrete does not let rainwater seep into the soil, so infiltration is reduced and less water reaches the groundwater.

heat-transfer.text: Why does a breeze blow from the land towards the sea at night?
options: The land cools faster than the sea, so warmer air above the sea rises and cooler air from the land moves in
The sea cools faster than the land, so air moves from the land to the sea
The Moon pulls the air towards the sea
Plants on land release air towards the sea at night
heat-transfer.explanation: At night the land cools faster than water, so the air over the sea is warmer and rises, and the cooler air from the land flows in to take its place.

heat-transfer.text: Why are the walls and roofs of many houses in hot places like Rajasthan painted white or in light colours?
options: Light colours absorb more heat and keep the house warm
Light colours make the walls stronger
Light colours reflect more sunlight, so the house absorbs less heat
Light colours stop air from entering the house
heat-transfer.explanation: Light-coloured surfaces reflect most of the sunlight falling on them, so the house stays cooler.

heat-transfer.text: Meena holds one end of a steel spoon while stirring hot dal on the stove. After a few minutes, the end she is holding becomes hot. How did the heat reach her fingers?
heat-transfer.explanation: Heat travelled along the steel spoon from its hot end to the cooler end she was holding, which is conduction.

heat-transfer.text: Ravi is at a beach in Chennai on a sunny afternoon. He notices that a cool breeze is blowing from the sea towards the land. Which statement correctly explains this?
options: Air above the land gets heated, rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in to take its place
Air above the sea gets heated, rises, and air from the land moves towards the sea
The waves of the sea push the air towards the land
Cool air falls from the clouds onto the land
heat-transfer.explanation: During the day land heats faster than the sea, so warm air over land rises and cooler sea air flows in, which is the sea breeze.

heat-transfer.text: Priya hangs her wet school uniform on a clothesline on a sunny and windy day. By evening it is completely dry. Which process dried the uniform?
heat-transfer.explanation: Heat from the Sun changed the water in the cloth into water vapour, which is evaporation, and the wind carried the vapour away.

heat-transfer.text: A village well had plenty of water during the monsoon, but by the end of May it became completely dry, even though the well was not damaged. What is the best explanation?
options: The water in the well froze in summer
The well water changed into groundwater by condensation
The water table went down below the bottom of the well
The rain in the monsoon was too heavy
heat-transfer.explanation: In summer there is little rain to recharge the ground while water keeps being used, so the water table falls below the bottom of the well.

heat-transfer.text: On a humid day, Aman takes a glass of ice-cold water out of the fridge. After a few minutes, tiny drops of water appear on the outside of the glass. Where do these drops come from?
options: Water leaking out through the glass
Water from the ice melting through the glass
Water produced by the glass itself
Water vapour in the air condensing on the cold surface of the glass
heat-transfer.explanation: Water vapour in the surrounding air cools on touching the cold glass and condenses into droplets on its outer surface.

heat-transfer.text: Kabir has to fix a room heater in a cold room so that the whole room warms up evenly. Where should he place it, and why?
options: Near the ceiling, because warm air sinks to the floor
Near the ceiling, because heat travels only downward
Near the floor, because the warm air rises and sets up convection currents in the room
Near the floor, because the floor conducts heat to the ceiling
heat-transfer.explanation: Air warmed near the floor rises while cooler air comes down to be heated, so convection currents warm the whole room.

heat-transfer.text: Assertion (A): Woollen clothes keep us warm in winter. Reason (R): Wool is a good conductor of heat.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
heat-transfer.explanation: Wool keeps us warm because it is a poor conductor and traps air, which is also a poor conductor, so the Reason is false.

heat-transfer.text: Assertion (A): Metal pans are used to cook food quickly. Reason (R): Air is a poor conductor of heat.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
heat-transfer.explanation: Both statements are true, but pans cook food quickly because metals are good conductors, not because air is a poor conductor.

heat-transfer.text: Assertion (A): Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by convection. Reason (R): The space between the Sun and the Earth has almost no air or other particles.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
heat-transfer.explanation: Convection needs moving particles, and since space has almost none, the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation, so A is false while R is true.

heat-transfer.text: Which of these is NOT a good conductor of heat?
heat-transfer.explanation: Iron, aluminium and copper are metals that conduct heat well, while glass is a poor conductor.

heat-transfer.text: Which of these is NOT a form of precipitation?
heat-transfer.explanation: Dew forms when water vapour condenses on cool surfaces near the ground, while rain, hail and snow fall from clouds.

heat-transfer.text: Which of these statements about radiation is NOT correct?
options: Radiation needs particles of a medium to carry heat
Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by radiation
Radiation can take place even through empty space
We feel the warmth of a fire sitting beside it mainly due to radiation
heat-transfer.explanation: Radiation does not need any medium, which is why the Sun's heat can reach us through space.

time-and-motion.text: Which ancient device measured time using the changing position of a shadow cast by the sun?
time-and-motion.explanation: A sundial uses the shadow of an object, cast by sunlight, to determine the time of day.

time-and-motion.text: What is the SI unit of time?
time-and-motion.explanation: The standard international (SI) unit for measuring time is the second, and its symbol is s.

time-and-motion.text: What is the name of the small metallic ball suspended by a thread in a simple pendulum?
time-and-motion.explanation: The small metallic ball at the end of a pendulum's thread is called the bob.

time-and-motion.text: How is the speed of an object calculated?
options: Total distance minus total time taken
Total time taken divided by total distance
Total distance multiplied by total time
Total distance divided by total time taken
time-and-motion.explanation: The speed of an object is calculated by dividing the total distance it covered by the total time it took.

time-and-motion.text: Which instrument in a vehicle measures the total distance it has travelled?
time-and-motion.explanation: An odometer is the instrument in a vehicle that measures the total distance travelled.

time-and-motion.text: What is the term for the time a pendulum takes to complete one full swing back and forth?
time-and-motion.explanation: The time period of a pendulum is the time it takes to complete one oscillation.

time-and-motion.text: What is the SI unit of speed?
time-and-motion.explanation: Since speed is distance divided by time, its SI unit is the SI unit of distance (metre) divided by the SI unit of time (second), which is metre/second (m/s).

time-and-motion.text: An object is said to be in uniform linear motion if it moves along a straight line and...
options: starts fast and then slows down.
covers unequal distances in equal time intervals.
covers equal distances in equal time intervals.
time-and-motion.explanation: Uniform linear motion is defined as an object moving in a straight line covering equal distances in equal intervals of time, meaning it has a constant speed.

time-and-motion.text: What is the function of a speedometer in a car?
options: To measure the time taken for a trip.
To measure and display the vehicle's speed.
time-and-motion.explanation: A speedometer is an instrument that measures and displays the current speed of a vehicle, usually in km/h.

time-and-motion.text: If two people run for the same amount of time, how can you tell which one is faster?
options: The one who covered less distance.
The one who covered more distance.
The one who has a heavier build.
time-and-motion.explanation: A faster person is someone who covers more distance in the same given interval of time.

time-and-motion.text: Which ancient time-measuring device worked based on the flow of sand from one bulb to another?
time-and-motion.explanation: An hourglass measures time based on the principle of a fixed amount of sand flowing from an upper bulb to a lower one.

time-and-motion.text: A bicycle travels 3.6 km in 15 minutes. What is its speed in m/s?
time-and-motion.explanation: To find the speed in m/s, convert distance to metres (3.6 km = 3600 m) and time to seconds (15 min = 900 s). Speed = 3600 m / 900 s = 4 m/s.

time-and-motion.text: When is an object's motion described as non-uniform linear motion?
options: When it moves in a circle at a constant speed.
When it moves along a straight line at a constant speed.
When it moves along a straight line with a changing speed.
time-and-motion.explanation: Non-uniform linear motion occurs when an object moves along a straight line but its speed is not constant; it keeps changing.

time-and-motion.text: What was Galileo Galilei's key conclusion after experimenting with pendulums?
options: The time for one swing is always the same for a pendulum of a given length.
The time for one swing depends on the mass of the bob.
The time for one swing decreases as the pendulum swings.
The time for one swing depends on how far it is pushed.
time-and-motion.explanation: Galileo concluded that for a pendulum of a specific length, the time period (time for one oscillation) is constant.

time-and-motion.text: An experiment is done by measuring the time period of several pendulums. What factor is found to affect the time period?
options: The time of day the experiment is done
time-and-motion.explanation: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on its length, but not on the mass of the bob.

time-and-motion.text: What is one complete to-and-fro movement of a pendulum bob called?
time-and-motion.explanation: When the bob moves from one end to the other and comes back, it completes one oscillation.

time-and-motion.text: How many seconds are there in one hour?
time-and-motion.explanation: One hour has 60 minutes and each minute has 60 seconds, so 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.

time-and-motion.text: Which unit is commonly used to show the speed of buses and cars on Indian roads?
time-and-motion.explanation: Road vehicles usually show speed in kilometres per hour on their speedometers and on speed limit boards.

time-and-motion.text: Which ancient device measured time using the steady flow of water out of or into a vessel?
time-and-motion.explanation: A water clock measures time by the steady flow of water, and in India a type of water clock called ghatika was used.

time-and-motion.text: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
time-and-motion.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 km ÷ 2 h = 60 km/h.

time-and-motion.text: A scooter is moving at 72 km/h. What is its speed in metres per second?
A boy walks at a speed of 1.5 m/s for 10 minutes. How much distance does he cover?
time-and-motion.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 1.5 m/s × 600 s = 900 m.

time-and-motion.text: A train moves at a speed of 90 km/h. How much time will it take to cover 270 km?
time-and-motion.explanation: Time = distance ÷ speed = 270 km ÷ 90 km/h = 3 hours.

time-and-motion.text: If the length of the thread of a simple pendulum is increased, what happens to its time period?
time-and-motion.explanation: A longer pendulum takes more time to complete one oscillation, so its time period increases.

time-and-motion.text: Which of these is an example of uniform linear motion?
options: A car moving on a straight highway with its speedometer showing a steady 50 km/h
A ball rolling on the ground and slowly coming to a stop
A bus moving on a straight road and stopping at every bus stop
A child going round and round on a merry-go-round
time-and-motion.explanation: The car moves along a straight line and covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its motion is uniform linear motion.

time-and-motion.text: A cyclist covers 6 km in the first 30 minutes and then 4 km in the next 20 minutes. What is the cyclist's speed for the whole journey (total distance divided by total time)?
time-and-motion.explanation: Total distance is 10 km and total time is 50 minutes, so speed = 10 km ÷ (50/60) h = 12 km/h.

time-and-motion.text: The time period of a pendulum is 2 seconds. How much time will it take to complete 15 oscillations?
time-and-motion.explanation: Total time = number of oscillations × time period = 15 × 2 s = 30 s.

time-and-motion.text: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 32 seconds. What is its time period?
time-and-motion.explanation: Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations = 32 s ÷ 20 = 1.6 s.

time-and-motion.text: Anu's grandfather says that in olden days people in villages guessed the time of day by looking at the shadow of a tree or a pole. At which time of the day is the shadow of a pole the shortest?
time-and-motion.explanation: Around noon the Sun is highest in the sky, so shadows are the shortest.

time-and-motion.text: Before a family trip, the odometer of Mr. Sharma's car showed 24350 km. When they reached their destination after 3 hours, it showed 24530 km. What was the speed of the car for the trip?
time-and-motion.explanation: Distance = 24530 − 24350 = 180 km, so speed = 180 km ÷ 3 h = 60 km/h.

time-and-motion.text: During sports day, Sita runs 100 m in 20 seconds and Gita runs 150 m in 25 seconds. Who is faster?
options: It cannot be decided because the distances are different
time-and-motion.explanation: Sita's speed is 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s and Gita's speed is 150 ÷ 25 = 6 m/s, so Gita is faster.

time-and-motion.text: Rahul's school bus moves along a straight road. He notices that the speedometer shows 40 km/h at some times, 0 km/h at traffic signals, and 30 km/h at other times. How can the motion of the bus be described?
options: Uniform motion because the road is straight
time-and-motion.explanation: The bus moves along a straight line but its speed keeps changing, so its motion is non-uniform linear motion.

time-and-motion.text: Tara makes two pendulums with threads of the same length. One has a light plastic bob and the other has a heavy iron bob. She measures the time period of both at the same place. What will she find?
options: The heavy bob has a much longer time period
The light bob has a much longer time period
Both have nearly the same time period
The heavy bob does not oscillate at all
time-and-motion.explanation: The time period of a pendulum depends on its length and not on the mass of the bob, so both have nearly the same time period.

time-and-motion.text: A train leaves a station at 6:00 am and reaches another city 200 km away at 8:30 am. What is the speed of the train?
time-and-motion.explanation: Time taken is 2.5 hours, so speed = 200 km ÷ 2.5 h = 80 km/h.

time-and-motion.text: Assertion (A): Pendulums were used to make clocks. Reason (R): A pendulum of a fixed length takes the same time for every oscillation at a given place.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
time-and-motion.explanation: Because each oscillation of a pendulum of fixed length takes the same time, pendulums could be used to keep regular time in clocks.

time-and-motion.text: Assertion (A): A car going round a circular track with its speedometer showing a steady 60 km/h is in uniform linear motion. Reason (R): The speed of the car is not changing.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
time-and-motion.explanation: The car's speed is constant, but it is moving in a circle and not in a straight line, so its motion is not linear.

time-and-motion.text: Assertion (A): An odometer shows the distance travelled by a vehicle. Reason (R): An odometer shows the speed of the vehicle at every moment.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
time-and-motion.explanation: The odometer measures distance travelled, while it is the speedometer that shows speed at every moment.

time-and-motion.text: Which of these is NOT a device used for measuring time?
time-and-motion.explanation: An odometer measures the distance travelled by a vehicle, while the others measure time.

time-and-motion.text: Which of these is NOT a correct relation between units?
time-and-motion.explanation: One hour has 3600 seconds, not 360 seconds.

time-and-motion.text: Which of these statements about a simple pendulum is NOT correct?
options: Using a heavier bob makes the time period shorter
The time period is the time taken to complete one oscillation
A longer pendulum has a longer time period
The time period can be found by timing 20 oscillations and dividing the time by 20
time-and-motion.explanation: The time period of a pendulum does not depend on the mass of the bob, so a heavier bob does not make it shorter.

life-processes-animals.text: Which of the following are all considered life processes essential for the survival of living beings?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Processes essential for survival, such as nutrition, respiration, excretion, and reproduction, are collectively called life processes.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the initial breakdown of food into smaller pieces by the processes of crushing and chewing called?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The process of initial breakdown of food into fine pieces by the teeth is called mechanical digestion.

life-processes-animals.text: Why does starchy food like rice start to taste sweet after being chewed for a long time?
options: The tongue adds a sweet substance to the food.
The food mixes with air and becomes sweet.
Saliva contains a digestive juice that breaks down starch into sugar.
The teeth release sugar into the food.
life-processes-animals.explanation: Saliva contains a digestive juice that helps break down starch, which is a type of carbohydrate, into sugar.

life-processes-animals.text: In an experiment, iodine solution is added to a test tube containing boiled rice that has been chewed for a minute. What is the expected result?
options: The solution shows little to no color change.
life-processes-animals.explanation: Saliva breaks down the starch in the chewed rice into simple sugars. Since iodine tests for the presence of starch, there will be no significant color change.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the function of the mucus secreted by the inner lining of the stomach?
options: To kill harmful bacteria in the food.
To protect the stomach lining from acid.
To break down proteins into simpler components.
To absorb nutrients from the partially digested food.
life-processes-animals.explanation: The mucus protects the stomach lining from the acid secreted in the stomach, preventing damage.

life-processes-animals.text: Which part of the human alimentary canal is the longest, measuring almost 6 metres?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

life-processes-animals.text: Bile is a digestive secretion from the liver. What are its main functions?
options: To neutralize acids from the stomach and break down fats.
To absorb water and salts from undigested food.
To make the food in the small intestine more acidic.
life-processes-animals.explanation: Bile neutralises acids present in the food moving down from the stomach and breaks down fats into tiny droplets, making its digestion easier.

life-processes-animals.text: The inner lining of the small intestine has thousands of finger-like projections called villi. What is their purpose?
options: To increase the surface area for efficient nutrient absorption.
To move food along the intestine.
life-processes-animals.explanation: The finger-like projections, or villi, increase the surface area of the small intestine for efficient nutrient absorption into the blood.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the main function of the large intestine in the digestive system?
options: To complete the digestion of proteins and fats.
To absorb water and some salts from undigested food.
To secrete bile and pancreatic juice.
To store food before it enters the stomach.
life-processes-animals.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and some salts from the undigested food, thus making the waste semi-solid.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the process called when grass-eating animals like cows bring partially digested food back from the stomach to the mouth for further chewing?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The process where partially digested food is brought back to the mouth for gradual chewing is called rumination, and these animals are called ruminants.

life-processes-animals.text: How do birds, which do not have teeth, mechanically break down their food?
options: Using a muscular chamber called a gizzard.
By swallowing strong acids that dissolve it.
Using a very strong beak to crush it.
life-processes-animals.explanation: Birds have a chamber called a gizzard where food is broken down by contraction and relaxation of its walls, often with the help of grit.

life-processes-animals.text: What happens to the ribs and diaphragm when we inhale (breathe in)?
options: The ribs move down and inwards, and the diaphragm moves up.
The ribs move down and inwards, and the diaphragm moves down.
The ribs move up and outwards, and the diaphragm moves down.
The ribs move up and outwards, and the diaphragm moves up.
life-processes-animals.explanation: During inhalation, the chest expands as the ribs move up and outwards and the diaphragm moves downwards, increasing the space inside the chest for air to enter.

life-processes-animals.text: What causes air to be pushed out of the lungs during exhalation (breathing out)?
options: The alveoli actively pump the air out.
The diaphragm moves down, increasing chest space.
The ribs move up and outwards, pulling air out.
The ribs move down and inwards, and the diaphragm moves up, reducing chest space.
life-processes-animals.explanation: When you exhale, the ribs move down and inwards, and the diaphragm moves upwards, reducing space in the chest and pushing air out of the lungs.

life-processes-animals.text: When exhaled air is blown through a straw into lime water, the lime water turns milky. What does this indicate?
options: Exhaled air is colder than inhaled air.
Exhaled air contains more oxygen than inhaled air.
Exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than inhaled air.
Exhaled air contains more water vapor.
life-processes-animals.explanation: Lime water turns milky when it reacts with carbon dioxide. This experiment shows that exhaled air contains more carbon dioxide than the air we inhale.

life-processes-animals.text: Where in the lungs does the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air and the blood take place?
options: In the small, balloon-like sacs called alveoli
life-processes-animals.explanation: The exchange of gases occurs in the alveoli, where oxygen passes from the air into the blood, and carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the process of taking food into the body called?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Taking food into the body through the mouth is called ingestion.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the removal of undigested food from the body through the anus called?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Undigested food is thrown out of the body through the anus, and this is called egestion.

life-processes-animals.text: Which tube carries food from the mouth to the stomach?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The food pipe, or oesophagus, carries swallowed food from the mouth to the stomach.

life-processes-animals.text: Which gas from the air is used by the cells of our body to release energy from food?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Body cells use oxygen to break down food and release energy.

life-processes-animals.text: Which acid is produced in our stomach that helps in digestion and kills many germs present in food?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid, which helps digestion and kills many germs in food.

life-processes-animals.text: Into which part of the alimentary canal does the pancreas release its digestive juice?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Pancreatic juice is poured into the small intestine, where it helps digest carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

life-processes-animals.text: What is assimilation?
options: Removing undigested food from the body
Taking in air through the nose
Use of absorbed nutrients by the body cells for energy, growth and repair
life-processes-animals.explanation: After absorption, nutrients reach body cells and are used to make new materials and release energy, which is assimilation.

life-processes-animals.text: What is the breakdown of food (glucose) using oxygen inside the cells to release energy called?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Respiration is the process in cells in which food is broken down using oxygen to release energy.

life-processes-animals.text: Which is the correct order in which food passes through the human alimentary canal?
options: Mouth, stomach, oesophagus, large intestine, small intestine, anus
Mouth, oesophagus, small intestine, stomach, large intestine, anus
Mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus
Mouth, small intestine, stomach, oesophagus, large intestine, anus
life-processes-animals.explanation: Food goes from the mouth to the oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine and is finally egested through the anus.

life-processes-animals.text: Which statement correctly tells the difference between breathing and respiration?
options: Breathing is taking in and giving out air, while respiration is the breakdown of food in cells to release energy
Breathing and respiration are exactly the same process
Breathing happens only in cells, while respiration happens only in the lungs
Breathing releases energy, while respiration only moves air in and out
life-processes-animals.explanation: Breathing moves air in and out of the lungs, while respiration takes place inside cells where food is broken down to release energy.

life-processes-animals.text: How do fish take in oxygen?
options: Through lungs, by coming out of water
Through small holes on the sides of their body
Through gills, which take in oxygen dissolved in water
life-processes-animals.explanation: Fish use gills to take in the oxygen that is dissolved in water.

life-processes-animals.text: An earthworm does not have lungs. How does it breathe?
options: It does not need oxygen at all
life-processes-animals.explanation: An earthworm exchanges gases through its moist skin, which is why it needs to stay in damp soil.

life-processes-animals.text: How does a cockroach take in air for breathing?
options: Through small openings called spiracles on the sides of its body, connected to air tubes
life-processes-animals.explanation: Insects like cockroaches have spiracles on the sides of their body that lead into a network of air tubes.

life-processes-animals.text: After running a 400 m race on sports day, Arjun notices that he is breathing much faster than usual. Why does this happen?
options: His lungs have become smaller after running
His body needs more oxygen to release more energy for the muscles
He has eaten too much food
Running reduces the amount of air in the atmosphere
life-processes-animals.explanation: During exercise the muscles need more energy, so the body takes in more oxygen by breathing faster.

life-processes-animals.text: Ramesh's grandfather has lost most of his teeth. He finds it hard to eat whole roasted chana and prefers soft, mashed food. Which step of digestion is mainly affected because of his missing teeth?
options: Absorption of food in the small intestine
Removal of water in the large intestine
Breaking food into small pieces in the mouth
life-processes-animals.explanation: Teeth crush and chew food into small pieces in the mouth, so without teeth this mechanical breakdown becomes difficult.

life-processes-animals.text: Neha notices that the fish in her aquarium keep coming up to the surface of the water and opening their mouths. The water has not been changed for many days and the air pump is not working. What is the most likely reason?
options: The water has too little dissolved oxygen
The fish want to eat food floating on top
The water has become too cold
The fish are trying to drink more water
life-processes-animals.explanation: Fish come to the surface when the water has too little dissolved oxygen for them to breathe through their gills.

life-processes-animals.text: Asha feels very weak after a long walk in the sun. Her mother gives her a glass of glucose water, and she feels better within a short time. Why does glucose give energy so quickly?
options: Glucose is digested in the mouth by saliva
Glucose goes directly into the lungs
Glucose is stored in the large intestine
Glucose does not need to be digested and is absorbed directly into the blood
life-processes-animals.explanation: Glucose is already a simple food, so it is absorbed into the blood without digestion and quickly reaches cells for respiration.

life-processes-animals.text: On a cold morning, Kiran breathes out onto a mirror and notices that a thin misty layer forms on it. What does this show about the air we breathe out?
options: It contains a lot of oxygen
life-processes-animals.explanation: The water vapour in exhaled air condenses on the cool mirror and forms a misty layer.

life-processes-animals.text: In winter, a frog may stay at the bottom of a pond for a long time without coming up for air. How does it get oxygen during this time?
options: Through its moist skin, from the water
It does not need any oxygen in winter
life-processes-animals.explanation: Frogs can take in oxygen dissolved in water through their thin, moist skin.

life-processes-animals.text: Assertion (A): We breathe faster while climbing stairs. Reason (R): Our muscles need more energy while climbing, so the body needs more oxygen.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-animals.explanation: Climbing makes muscles work harder, so more oxygen is needed to release energy, and breathing speeds up to supply it.

life-processes-animals.text: Assertion (A): The small intestine is the longest part of the alimentary canal. Reason (R): Most of the absorption of digested food takes place in the large intestine.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-animals.explanation: The small intestine is the longest part, but most digested food is absorbed in the small intestine, not the large intestine.

life-processes-animals.text: Assertion (A): Saliva helps in the digestion of starch. Reason (R): The tongue helps us taste food.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-animals.explanation: Both statements are true, but the tongue's role in tasting does not explain how saliva digests starch.

life-processes-animals.text: Which of these is NOT a part of the alimentary canal?
life-processes-animals.explanation: The liver is a digestive gland that releases bile, but food does not pass through it.

life-processes-animals.text: Which of these animals is NOT a ruminant (an animal that chews the cud)?
life-processes-animals.explanation: Cows, buffaloes and goats chew the cud, but horses do not.

life-processes-animals.text: Which of these is NOT a function of the stomach?
options: Absorbing most of the digested food into the blood
Killing many germs in food with acid
Holding food for some time while it is churned
life-processes-animals.explanation: Most absorption of digested food happens in the small intestine, not in the stomach.

life-processes-plants.text: Which of the following, together, are essential for growth?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Food provides nutrients like carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and minerals, which, along with water, are all essential for growth.

life-processes-plants.text: What is the green pigment in plant leaves that helps in capturing sunlight?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Leaves are mostly green because of the presence of a green pigment called chlorophyll, that helps in capturing sunlight efficiently.

life-processes-plants.text: What is the process by which plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to create their own food?
life-processes-plants.explanation: The process by which plants prepare food in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll using carbon dioxide and water is called photosynthesis.

life-processes-plants.text: What are the tiny pores, usually on the surface of leaves, that help in the exchange of gases?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Tiny pores on the surface of leaves, called stomata, help in the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

life-processes-plants.text: Which gas is released by plants during photosynthesis?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Oxygen is released during the process of photosynthesis. An experiment shows this gas can cause a lit matchstick to produce an intense flame.

life-processes-plants.text: What is the purpose of boiling a leaf in alcohol before testing it for starch with iodine?
options: To add nutrients to the leaf
To remove the green pigment chlorophyll
To kill any bacteria on the leaf
life-processes-plants.explanation: Decolourisation of a leaf by removing chlorophyll enables us to easily observe the colour change from the iodine test, and thus, the presence of starch.

life-processes-plants.text: An experiment is set up with three pots: Pot A (sunlight, water), Pot B (sunlight, no water), and Pot C (dark, water). Which plant is expected to show the most growth?
life-processes-plants.explanation: The results of the experiment indicate that plants require both sunlight and water for their growth, so the plant with both will grow best.

life-processes-plants.text: What color change indicates the presence of starch when iodine solution is added to a decolourised leaf?
life-processes-plants.explanation: If the colour of the leaf changes to blue-black after adding diluted iodine solution, it indicates the presence of starch.

life-processes-plants.text: What is the food produced during photosynthesis, which is a simple carbohydrate that can be converted to starch for storage?
life-processes-plants.explanation: During photosynthesis, food is actually produced in the form of glucose, a simple carbohydrate, which later gets converted into starch for storage.

life-processes-plants.text: Which tissue in a plant is responsible for transporting water and minerals from the roots to the other parts of the plant?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Water and minerals are transported to the leaves and other parts of plants through the thin tube-like structure called the xylem.

life-processes-plants.text: Which tissue transports the food prepared in the leaves to all other parts of the plant?
life-processes-plants.explanation: The food prepared by plants in the leaves is transported to all parts of the plant through another set of thin tube-like structures called the phloem.

life-processes-plants.text: What are the products of the process of respiration in plants?
life-processes-plants.explanation: During respiration, glucose is broken down in the presence of oxygen, releasing carbon dioxide, water, and energy.

life-processes-plants.text: In an experiment, half of a leaf is enclosed in a bottle containing caustic soda (which absorbs carbon dioxide). After being in sunlight, which part of the leaf will test positive for starch?
life-processes-plants.explanation: The part of the leaf outside the bottle has access to carbon dioxide and will produce starch, while the part inside will not because carbon dioxide is essential for photosynthesis.

life-processes-plants.text: A leaf with both green and non-green patches is kept in sunlight and then tested for starch. What is the expected result?
options: The entire leaf will turn blue-black.
Only the green patches will turn blue-black.
There will be no change in color.
Only the non-green patches will turn blue-black.
life-processes-plants.explanation: Starch is produced only in the green patches where chlorophyll is present to perform photosynthesis. Therefore, only these patches will turn blue-black with iodine.

life-processes-plants.text: An experiment with germinating seeds shows that the air they release turns limewater milky. What does this demonstrate?
options: Seeds use carbon dioxide for germination.
Seeds produce carbon dioxide during respiration.
life-processes-plants.explanation: Limewater turns milky due to the presence of carbon dioxide. The experiment shows that additional carbon dioxide is produced by the seeds as they respire.

life-processes-plants.text: In which part of a leaf cell is the green pigment chlorophyll found?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Chlorophyll is present inside small green bodies called chloroplasts in leaf cells.

life-processes-plants.text: Which raw materials does a green plant take in to make its food by photosynthesis?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil to make glucose in the presence of sunlight.

life-processes-plants.text: Which part of a plant mainly absorbs water from the soil?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Roots, especially the fine root hairs, absorb water and minerals from the soil.

life-processes-plants.text: Why do gardeners loosen the soil around plants from time to time?
options: So that the roots get enough air to respire
So that the leaves get more sunlight
So that the plant stops making food
life-processes-plants.explanation: Loose soil has more air spaces, so roots get the oxygen they need for respiration.

life-processes-plants.text: When do plants carry out respiration?
options: All the time, both day and night
Only when there is no sunlight
life-processes-plants.explanation: Like all living things, plants respire all the time to get energy from food.

life-processes-plants.text: The glucose made in leaves is mostly stored in plants in the form of:
life-processes-plants.explanation: Extra glucose is changed into starch, which is stored in leaves, stems, roots and seeds.

life-processes-plants.text: Which word equation correctly shows photosynthesis?
options: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (in sunlight, with chlorophyll)
life-processes-plants.explanation: In photosynthesis, carbon dioxide and water combine using sunlight and chlorophyll to form glucose, and oxygen is released.

life-processes-plants.text: Before doing a starch test on a leaf, why is the potted plant kept in a dark room for two to three days?
options: To use up the starch already present in the leaves
To increase the amount of chlorophyll
life-processes-plants.explanation: In the dark the plant cannot make new food, so it uses up the stored starch and the leaves become starch-free before the experiment.

life-processes-plants.text: The leaves of red amaranth (lal saag) are reddish in colour. Which statement about them is correct?
options: They cannot make food because they have no chlorophyll
They make food only at night
They take ready-made food from the soil
They have chlorophyll, but its green colour is hidden by red pigments
life-processes-plants.explanation: Reddish leaves also contain chlorophyll and make food; other red pigments simply hide the green colour.

life-processes-plants.text: A carrot stores food in its root. Through which tissue does the food made in the leaves reach the root?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Phloem carries food made in the leaves to all other parts of the plant, including the roots.

life-processes-plants.text: Which gas do plants take in during respiration?
life-processes-plants.explanation: During respiration, plants use oxygen to break down glucose and release energy.

life-processes-plants.text: In bright sunlight, a green plant gives out more oxygen than it uses. Why?
options: Photosynthesis makes oxygen faster than respiration uses it
The plant stops respiring during the day
The roots release extra oxygen into the air
Oxygen gets stored in the starch
life-processes-plants.explanation: In bright light, photosynthesis produces oxygen much faster than respiration uses it, so extra oxygen is given out.

life-processes-plants.text: A cactus has spines in place of broad leaves. Which part of the cactus mainly carries out photosynthesis?
life-processes-plants.explanation: The green stem of a cactus contains chlorophyll, so it makes food for the plant.

life-processes-plants.text: Meena placed a water plant, Hydrilla, in a glass of water kept in bright sunlight. After some time, she saw tiny bubbles rising from its leaves. When she moved the glass to a dark room, the bubbles almost stopped. Which gas were the bubbles mainly made of?
life-processes-plants.explanation: In sunlight Hydrilla carries out photosynthesis and gives out oxygen, which forms the bubbles.

life-processes-plants.text: Raju's grandmother kept a small potted plant inside a closed cupboard for a week. When she took it out, the plant looked pale and weak. What is the most likely reason?
options: It got too much carbon dioxide
It could not get sunlight to make its food
life-processes-plants.explanation: Without sunlight a plant cannot carry out photosynthesis, so it cannot make food and becomes weak.

life-processes-plants.text: After heavy rain, Kiran's field stayed flooded with water for many days. The crop plants began to wilt and die even though there was plenty of water. What is the best explanation?
options: The roots could not get enough oxygen for respiration in the waterlogged soil
The leaves got too much sunlight
The plants made too much food
The stomata absorbed too much water
life-processes-plants.explanation: Water fills the air spaces in the soil, so roots do not get oxygen to respire and the plants suffer.

life-processes-plants.text: Anil kept a potted plant in the dark for three days. Then he coated both surfaces of one leaf with petroleum jelly and kept the plant in sunlight for a day. When he tested the coated leaf with iodine, it did not turn blue-black. Why?
options: The leaf lost all its chlorophyll
Water could not reach the leaf through the xylem
The jelly blocked the stomata, so carbon dioxide could not enter the leaf
Iodine does not react with starch in coated leaves
life-processes-plants.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters leaves through stomata, so blocking them stopped photosynthesis and no starch was made.

life-processes-plants.text: Priya noticed that someone had removed a complete ring of bark from around the trunk of a tree in her colony. After some weeks, the roots of the tree began to starve. Which tissue, present just inside the bark, was removed along with it?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Phloem lies close to the bark and carries food from the leaves down to the roots, so removing it starves the roots.

life-processes-plants.text: Ravi's mother waters the tulsi plant only at its base, yet the leaves at the top stay fresh. Which tissue carries the water up to the leaves?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Xylem carries water and minerals from the roots up to the stem and leaves.

life-processes-plants.text: Assertion (A): Leaves are called the food factories of a plant. Reason (R): Leaves contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-plants.explanation: Leaves make food because they have chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, so R correctly explains A.

life-processes-plants.text: Assertion (A): A plant kept in complete darkness for a few days has very little starch left in its leaves. Reason (R): Plants do not respire in darkness.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-plants.explanation: In darkness the plant keeps respiring and uses up its starch without making new food, so A is true but R is false.

life-processes-plants.text: Assertion (A): Green plants get their food ready-made from the soil. Reason (R): Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
life-processes-plants.explanation: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so A is false, while it is true that roots absorb water and minerals.

life-processes-plants.text: Which of these is NOT needed by a plant for photosynthesis?
life-processes-plants.explanation: Oxygen is not a raw material for photosynthesis; it is given out as a product.

life-processes-plants.text: Which of these is NOT a function of stomata?
options: Letting carbon dioxide enter the leaf
Letting oxygen go out of the leaf
Letting water vapour escape from the leaf
life-processes-plants.explanation: Water is absorbed from the soil by roots, while stomata allow exchange of gases and loss of water vapour.

life-processes-plants.text: Which of these plant parts does NOT usually carry out photosynthesis?
options: Green leaf of a mango tree
Green leaf of a spinach plant
life-processes-plants.explanation: A carrot root grows underground and has no chlorophyll, so it only stores food and does not make it.

light-shadows.text: Which of the following is a non-luminous object?
light-shadows.explanation: Non-luminous objects do not emit their own light. The Moon is a non-luminous object that shines by reflecting the light from the Sun.

light-shadows.text: An activity shows that a candle flame can be seen through a straight pipe but not through a bent one. What does this observation suggest?
options: Light travels in a straight line.
Light is a form of energy.
light-shadows.explanation: The inability to see the light through a bent pipe demonstrates that light travels in a straight line and cannot go around the bend.

light-shadows.text: What is a material called if it allows light to pass through it only partially?
light-shadows.explanation: Light passes partially through translucent materials. It passes almost completely through transparent materials and does not pass through opaque materials.

light-shadows.text: What three things are needed to observe a shadow?
options: A light source, a transparent object, and a wall
A mirror, a translucent object, and a screen
Only a light source and an opaque object
A light source, an opaque object, and a screen
light-shadows.explanation: To form a shadow, we need a source of light, an opaque object to block the light, and a screen on which the shadow is formed.

light-shadows.text: What is the change in the direction of light by a mirror called?
light-shadows.explanation: A shiny surface or a mirror changes the direction of light that falls upon it. This change in direction is called the reflection of light.

light-shadows.text: Which of the following is a key characteristic of the image formed by a plane mirror?
options: It can be obtained on a screen.
It is of the same size as the object.
It is smaller than the object.
light-shadows.explanation: The image formed by a plane mirror is of the same size as the object, is erect, and cannot be obtained on a screen.

light-shadows.text: In a plane mirror, the left side of an object appears as the right side of the image. What is this phenomenon called?
light-shadows.explanation: The perceived left-right reversal in the images formed by a plane mirror is called lateral inversion.

light-shadows.text: What kind of image is formed by a pinhole camera?
light-shadows.explanation: A pinhole camera creates an inverted (upside down) image of an object on a screen, and the image shows the colours of the object.

light-shadows.text: Which device uses two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box to allow someone to see over an obstacle?
light-shadows.explanation: A simple periscope can be made by placing two plane mirrors in a Z-shaped box, enabling a user to see objects that are not directly visible.

light-shadows.text: An object is placed between a fixed torch and a screen. What will happen to its shadow if the object is moved closer to the torch?
light-shadows.explanation: When an object is moved closer to the light source, keeping the screen fixed, the shadow it casts becomes larger.

light-shadows.text: Which of these objects forms the darkest shadow when placed in the path of light?
light-shadows.explanation: Opaque objects, like cardboard, block light completely and therefore form darker shadows than translucent or transparent objects.

light-shadows.text: What is the principle behind the working of a kaleidoscope?
options: Light travels in a straight line
light-shadows.explanation: A kaleidoscope uses three mirrors, and the multiple images formed due to reflections of reflections create many interesting patterns.

light-shadows.text: Which of the following statements about shadows is correct?
options: A shadow is a type of reflection.
Changing the colour of an opaque object does not change the colour of its shadow.
The color of the shadow depends on the color of the object.
light-shadows.explanation: A shadow is an area where light is blocked. Changing the colour of the opaque object does not change the colour of the shadow.

light-shadows.text: Which of these can form an image on a screen?
light-shadows.explanation: A pinhole camera forms an image on a screen, while the image formed by a plane mirror cannot be obtained on a screen.

light-shadows.text: If you stand 3 meters in front of a plane mirror, how far away does your image appear to be from you?
light-shadows.explanation: The image in a plane mirror appears to be as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. Therefore, the total distance is 3m (object to mirror) + 3m (mirror to image).

light-shadows.text: Which of these is a luminous object?
light-shadows.explanation: A firefly gives out its own light, so it is luminous.

light-shadows.text: Which of these is a natural source of light?
light-shadows.explanation: The Sun gives out light naturally, while tube lights, torches and candles are made by people.

light-shadows.text: Which of these materials is translucent?
light-shadows.explanation: Frosted glass lets only some light pass through, so objects behind it look blurred.

light-shadows.text: Why are we able to see a book lying on a table in daylight?
options: Our eyes give out light that falls on the book
Light falling on the book is reflected into our eyes
The book makes its own light
The air around the book glows
light-shadows.explanation: We see non-luminous objects when light falling on them is reflected and reaches our eyes.

light-shadows.text: The word AMBULANCE is often written in reverse on the front of an ambulance. Why?
options: So that drivers ahead can read it correctly in their rear-view mirrors
So that it can be read at night
Because all vehicles must write their names in reverse
light-shadows.explanation: A mirror laterally inverts the reversed word, so drivers ahead see AMBULANCE written correctly.

light-shadows.text: Which of these capital letters looks exactly the same when seen in a plane mirror?
light-shadows.explanation: H has identical left and right halves, so lateral inversion does not change how it looks.

light-shadows.text: A pinhole camera can form an image of an object because:
options: Mirrors inside the camera reflect light
light-shadows.explanation: Rays of light from each point of the object travel in straight lines through the pinhole and form an image on the screen.

light-shadows.text: A boy who is 1.4 m tall stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. What is the height of his image and how far is the image from the mirror?
options: 1.4 m tall and 2 m behind the mirror
0.7 m tall and 2 m behind the mirror
1.4 m tall and 4 m behind the mirror
2.8 m tall and 2 m behind the mirror
light-shadows.explanation: A plane mirror forms an image of the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.

light-shadows.text: How is the image of a flower in a plane mirror different from the shadow of the same flower?
options: The image is always dark, while the shadow shows colours
The image shows the colours and details of the flower, while the shadow is only a dark outline
The shadow is formed only by mirrors
light-shadows.explanation: A mirror image shows colour and details of the object, while a shadow only shows its dark outline.

light-shadows.text: In the early morning, the Sun is in the east. In which direction will the shadow of an electric pole fall?
light-shadows.explanation: A shadow forms on the side opposite to the light source, so with the Sun in the east the shadow falls towards the west.

light-shadows.text: Can you see a steel spoon in a completely dark room with no light at all?
options: No, because no light falls on it to be reflected into our eyes
Only if the spoon is very big
light-shadows.explanation: A non-luminous object is seen only when light reflected from it reaches our eyes, which cannot happen in total darkness.

light-shadows.text: What is the dark area formed behind an opaque object when it blocks light called?
light-shadows.explanation: A shadow is the dark region formed when an opaque object blocks the path of light.

light-shadows.text: In a pinhole camera, the image of a burning candle is seen on the screen. If the candle is moved closer to the pinhole, the image becomes:
light-shadows.explanation: A pinhole camera always forms an inverted image, and the image becomes larger as the object comes closer to the pinhole.

light-shadows.text: During a power cut, Aarav lit a candle and made shadow animals with his hands on the wall. He then moved his hands away from the candle and closer to the wall. What happened to the shadows?
light-shadows.explanation: When the object moves away from the light source and closer to the screen, it blocks less light and its shadow becomes smaller.

light-shadows.text: Neha's little brother stands in front of a dressing table mirror and raises his right hand. Which hand does his image appear to raise?
light-shadows.explanation: A plane mirror shows lateral inversion, so the right hand appears as the left hand in the image.

light-shadows.text: At a hair salon, Rohit sits facing a large mirror. The barber holds a small mirror behind Rohit's head, and Rohit can now see the back of his head in the large mirror. What does this show?
options: Light reflected by one mirror can be reflected again by another mirror
Mirrors absorb all the light falling on them
light-shadows.explanation: Light from the back of the head is reflected by the small mirror to the large mirror and then to Rohit's eyes.

light-shadows.text: Fatima looked at a lit street lamp first through a sheet of butter paper, then through a clear glass sheet and finally through a thick piece of cardboard. Which option correctly describes the three sheets in the order she used them?
light-shadows.explanation: Butter paper lets some light through (translucent), clear glass lets almost all light through (transparent) and cardboard lets no light through (opaque).

light-shadows.text: Tara wants to make a periscope using a long cardboard box and two plane mirrors so that she can see over a wall. How should she fix the mirrors?
options: Both mirrors flat at the bottom of the box
Both mirrors at right angles to each other at the top of the box
One at each end, parallel and facing each other, each tilted at 45 degrees
One mirror at the top and the other removed
light-shadows.explanation: In a periscope two parallel mirrors facing each other at 45 degrees reflect light down the tube to the eye.

light-shadows.text: Kabir stood in an open ground at 8 am and saw that his shadow was much longer than his height. At noon, his shadow was very short. What causes this change?
options: The change in the position of the Sun in the sky
The ground moves during the day
light-shadows.explanation: In the morning the Sun is low in the sky and casts long shadows, while near noon it is high overhead and casts short shadows.

light-shadows.text: Assertion (A): A shadow is formed on the side of an object opposite to the source of light. Reason (R): Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through an opaque object.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
light-shadows.explanation: Because light travels in straight lines and is blocked by the opaque object, a dark region forms behind it, so R explains A.

light-shadows.text: Assertion (A): The Moon is a luminous object. Reason (R): The Moon shines in the night sky by reflecting sunlight.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
light-shadows.explanation: The Moon does not make its own light, so it is non-luminous, but it does shine by reflecting sunlight.

light-shadows.text: Assertion (A): The image formed by a plane mirror cannot be obtained on a screen. Reason (R): The image formed by a plane mirror is of the same size as the object.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
light-shadows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the size of the image has nothing to do with whether it can be caught on a screen.

light-shadows.text: Which of these is NOT true about a shadow?
options: It forms on the side of the object away from the light source
It shows the colour of the object
It needs an opaque object to block light
light-shadows.explanation: A shadow is always dark whatever the colour of the object, so it does not show the object's colour.

light-shadows.text: Which of these does NOT use the reflection of light by mirrors?
light-shadows.explanation: A pinhole camera forms an image because light travels in straight lines through a small hole and does not use mirrors.

light-shadows.text: Find the odd one out based on how much light passes through them.
light-shadows.explanation: Butter paper is translucent, while glass, clean water and air are transparent.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why does the Sun appear to move across the sky from East to West?
options: Because the Earth is moving closer to and then farther from the Sun.
Because the Moon's gravity pulls the Sun across the sky.
Because the Earth is turning around on its own axis.
Because the Sun is orbiting the Earth.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Sun appears to be moving because we view it from the Earth, which is turning around itself.

earth-moon-sun.text: Approximately how long does it take for the Earth to complete one rotation on its axis?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth completes one rotation in about 24 hours.

earth-moon-sun.text: What is the primary cause of the day and night cycle on Earth?
options: The tilt of the Earth's axis.
The Moon blocking the Sun's light.
The Earth's revolution around the Sun.
The Earth's rotation from West to East.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth's rotation from West to East causes the day-night cycle.

earth-moon-sun.text: What is the term for the motion of an object around another object?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Revolution is the motion of an object around another object.

earth-moon-sun.text: A solar eclipse occurs when which celestial body comes in between the Sun and the Earth?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: At certain times, the Moon can come in between the Sun and the Earth in a way that obstructs the light from the Sun from reaching us, which is known as a solar eclipse.

earth-moon-sun.text: What happens during a lunar eclipse?
options: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon.
The Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon.
The Moon's shadow falls on the Sun.
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth comes in between the Sun and the Moon, blocking sunlight from reaching the Moon.

earth-moon-sun.text: When viewed from above the North Pole, in which direction does the Earth rotate?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: When viewed from the top of the North Pole, the Earth is rotating in the anti-clockwise direction, that is, from West to East.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why does the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara) appear to be nearly stationary in the sky?
options: It is the brightest star in the sky.
It is much closer to Earth than other stars.
It does not move like other stars.
The Earth's axis of rotation points very close to it.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth's axis of rotation points very close to the Pole Star in the Northern Hemisphere, therefore, the Pole Star appears nearly stationary.

earth-moon-sun.text: What are the two main factors that cause seasons on Earth?
options: The Earth's rotation and its revolution.
The number of solar eclipses and lunar eclipses.
The Earth's distance from the Sun and its speed of rotation.
The tilt of the Earth's axis and its spherical shape.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The tilt of the Earth's axis and the spherical shape of the Earth gives rise to seasons.

earth-moon-sun.text: How long does it take for the Earth to complete one revolution around the Sun?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in about 365 days and 6 hours.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why do we see different stars in the night sky during different months of the year?
options: Because of the changing seasons and weather.
Because the stars themselves are moving away.
Because of the Earth's daily rotation on its axis.
Because the Earth revolves around the Sun, changing our direction of view.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: As the Earth revolves around the Sun continuously, the stars seen in the night sky after sunset gradually change over a year as we look in different directions.

earth-moon-sun.text: What happens on the days of an equinox?
options: The Sun does not set at the poles.
The day is the longest of the year.
The night is the longest of the year.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Around 21 March and 23 September, the daytime lasts for 12 hours. These days are called the spring and the autumn equinox.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why is it dangerous to look directly at the Sun, even during a solar eclipse?
options: The Sun is still intense enough to damage the eyes and cause blindness.
The darkness makes your pupils too large.
It is only dangerous if you use a telescope.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Even during an eclipse, the Sun is intense enough to damage the eyes and cause blindness, so directly viewing it must be strictly avoided.

earth-moon-sun.text: If you are on a merry-go-round turning in an anti-clockwise direction, how will stationary objects like trees appear to move?
options: They will appear to move anti-clockwise.
They will appear to move towards you.
They will not appear to move at all.
They will appear to move in a clockwise direction.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: While you turn in the anti-clockwise direction, the objects appear to turn around you in the opposite direction, that is, in the clockwise direction.

earth-moon-sun.text: What is the term for the imaginary line that passes through an object, around which all its parts move in circles?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Rotation is the motion of an object in which all its parts move in circles around an imaginary line that passes through it. This line is called the axis of rotation.

earth-moon-sun.text: The spinning of the Earth on its own axis is called:
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Rotation is the spinning of the Earth about its own axis.

earth-moon-sun.text: In which direction does the Sun appear to rise every morning?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Because the Earth rotates from west to east, the Sun appears to rise in the east.

earth-moon-sun.text: Which of these gives out its own light?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Sun is a star and gives out its own light, while the Moon, Earth and Mars only reflect sunlight.

earth-moon-sun.text: In which direction does the Earth rotate on its axis?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth rotates from west to east, which is why the Sun and stars appear to move from east to west.

earth-moon-sun.text: The Moon revolves around the Earth. Around which body does the Earth, along with the Moon, revolve?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Earth revolves around the Sun, taking the Moon along with it.

earth-moon-sun.text: On which day of the month can a solar eclipse take place?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: A solar eclipse needs the Moon to be between the Sun and the Earth, which happens only on a new moon day.

earth-moon-sun.text: On which day of the month can a lunar eclipse take place?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: A lunar eclipse needs the Earth to be between the Sun and the Moon, which happens only on a full moon day.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why is it safe to watch a lunar eclipse with bare eyes?
options: Because the Moon is very far away
Because moonlight is only reflected sunlight and is much dimmer than direct sunlight
Because lunar eclipses happen only in the daytime
Because the Earth's shadow makes the Moon brighter
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Moon only reflects a small part of sunlight, so looking at it does not harm the eyes.

earth-moon-sun.text: The Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon, yet both look nearly the same size in our sky. Why?
options: The Sun is also about 400 times farther from the Earth than the Moon
The Moon is brighter than the Sun
The Sun shrinks during the day
The air around the Earth makes the Moon look bigger
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Objects look smaller when farther away, and the Sun is about 400 times farther than the Moon, so both appear nearly equal in size.

earth-moon-sun.text: Why does a solar eclipse NOT happen on every new moon day?
options: The Moon stops moving on new moon day
The Sun is too bright on new moon day
The Moon's path is slightly tilted, so it usually passes a little above or below the line joining the Sun and the Earth
The Earth stops rotating on new moon day
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Because the Moon's orbit is slightly tilted, the Sun, Moon and Earth come in an exact straight line only on some new moon days.

earth-moon-sun.text: The Sun rises earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat. Why?
options: Arunachal Pradesh is closer to the Sun
Arunachal Pradesh is in the east of India, and the Earth rotates from west to east
Arunachal Pradesh has taller mountains that touch the Sun
earth-moon-sun.explanation: As the Earth rotates from west to east, places in the east face the Sun first and see sunrise earlier.

earth-moon-sun.text: About how long does the Moon take to complete one revolution around the Earth?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Moon takes about 27 days to go once around the Earth.

earth-moon-sun.text: On a clear night, in which direction do the stars appear to move across the sky?
options: They do not appear to move at all
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Because the Earth rotates from west to east, stars appear to move from east to west across the night sky.

earth-moon-sun.text: Ananya is sitting in a moving train. She sees trees and electric poles outside appear to move backwards, though they are not moving. Which of these does her observation help us understand?
options: Why the Sun appears to move across the sky while the Earth rotates
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Just as the trees seem to move because the train moves, the Sun seems to move because the Earth rotates.

earth-moon-sun.text: On a full moon night, Kunal's family watched the Moon slowly darken from one side until it looked dull and reddish-brown. After some time, it became bright again. What caused the darkening?
options: The Earth's shadow falling on the Moon
Thick clouds in front of the Moon
The Sun's shadow falling on the Moon
earth-moon-sun.explanation: During a lunar eclipse, the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon and its shadow falls on the Moon.

earth-moon-sun.text: Zoya lives in Delhi. At 8 pm, she video-calls her aunt in New York, USA, where it is morning. Why is it morning in New York when it is night in Delhi?
options: The Earth is round and rotates, so only the half of the Earth facing the Sun has day at any time
The Sun moves around the Earth faster in the USA
New York is closer to the Moon
Clouds hide the Sun over Delhi
earth-moon-sun.explanation: As the round Earth rotates, different places face the Sun at different times, so some places have day while others have night.

earth-moon-sun.text: Pihu fixed a stick upright in an open ground and marked the tip of its shadow every hour from 9 am to 3 pm. The shadow became shorter until about noon and then longer again, and it shifted from the west side of the stick to the east side. What does this activity show?
options: The stick was growing during the day
The Sun stays at one fixed position in the sky
The position of the Sun in the sky appears to change during the day because the Earth rotates
The Earth stops rotating at noon
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The changing length and direction of the shadow show that the Sun's position in the sky changes through the day due to the Earth's rotation.

earth-moon-sun.text: Before a solar eclipse, Ravi's teacher told the class to watch it only through certified solar viewing glasses or by using a pinhole projection. Ravi asked if his ordinary sunglasses would be enough. What should the teacher say?
options: Yes, any dark sunglasses are safe
Yes, if he looks for only a few minutes
No, ordinary sunglasses do not block enough of the Sun's harmful light
Yes, if he looks through binoculars
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Ordinary sunglasses are not dark enough, so looking at the Sun through them can still damage the eyes.

earth-moon-sun.text: Imagine an astronaut standing on the Moon at the same time as a total lunar eclipse is seen from the Earth. She looks towards the Sun. What would she most likely see?
earth-moon-sun.explanation: During a lunar eclipse the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so from the Moon the Earth would be seen covering the Sun.

earth-moon-sun.text: Assertion (A): We do not feel the Earth rotating. Reason (R): The Earth rotates smoothly, and everything on it, including the air, moves along with it.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Since the Earth's motion is smooth and we move along with it, we do not feel any jerk, so R explains A.

earth-moon-sun.text: Assertion (A): The Sun goes around the Earth from east to west every day. Reason (R): The Earth rotates on its axis from west to east.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Sun only appears to move from east to west because the Earth rotates from west to east, so A is false and R is true.

earth-moon-sun.text: Assertion (A): A lunar eclipse can happen only on a full moon day. Reason (R): The Moon takes about 27 days to revolve once around the Earth.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Both are true, but A is explained by the Earth coming between the Sun and the Moon on full moon day, not by the time the Moon takes to revolve.

earth-moon-sun.text: Which of these is NOT caused by the rotation of the Earth?
options: The Sun appearing to rise in the east
Stars appearing to move across the night sky
The change of seasons during the year
earth-moon-sun.explanation: Seasons are caused by the Earth's revolution around the Sun along with the tilt of its axis, not by its rotation.

earth-moon-sun.text: Which of these does NOT happen during a lunar eclipse?
options: The Sun gets hidden behind the Moon
The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon passes through the Earth's shadow
It is a full moon night
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Sun being hidden behind the Moon is a solar eclipse; in a lunar eclipse the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

earth-moon-sun.text: Find the odd one out: the Sun, the Moon, the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara), Sirius.
earth-moon-sun.explanation: The Moon does not make its own light, while the Sun, the Pole Star and Sirius are all stars that give out light.
